metadata.name: escrow
metadata.description: Sealed: milestone-based escrow with USDC support

instructions.name: approve_refund
docs: Mutual refund, two-step: each party approves in their OWN transaction and
the refund executes once both have. Avoids the ~90s blockhash expiry that
made the single shared co-signed transaction unusable in practice.

accounts.name: signer
docs: The approving party — must be the deal's buyer or seller.

accounts.name: buyer_token_account
docs: Buyer's USDC account — the refund destination. Validated against the deal's
buyer + mint, so the caller can't redirect funds.

instructions.name: buyer_timeout_refund
docs: Unilateral refund after 30-day inactivity timeout (buyer only, no seller required)

instructions.name: cancel_deal
docs: Cancel an unfunded deal, close accounts, reclaim rent (buyer only)

instructions.name: clear_user_tier
docs: Revoke a wallet's tier (authority only), returning the account rent.

instructions.name: close_deal
docs: Close a completed or refunded deal, reclaim escrow vault rent (buyer only)

instructions.name: create_deal
docs: Create a new deal with milestones and escrow parameters.
`creator_wallet` records which party initiated the deal — it cannot be
inferred, since the buyer always signs regardless of who created it —
and selects whose tier (if any) prices the deal.

accounts.name: mint
docs: The deal's payment mint. Must be on the platform allowlist (USDC/USDT/
USDG) once one is set — enforced in the handler against `config`, since
the accepted set lives in Config data, not a compile-time constant (audit
H-1). An empty allowlist accepts any mint (pre-fix behavior).

accounts.name: config
docs: Global platform config. REQUIRED (audit C-1): when this was optional, a
hand-built tx could omit it and permanently snapshot fee_bps=0, bypassing
the platform fee entirely. It is now mandatory, so the fee snapshot always
reflects the real on-chain config. The config must be initialized
(`init_config`) before any deal — which it is on every live deployment.
A deal is still fee-FREE when the config's fee isn't active (no rate or no
treasury), so the pre-config fee-free era is preserved via config state,
not via omitting the account.

accounts.name: creator_tier
docs: The deal creator's tier assignment, if they have one. Optional because
ABSENCE IS THE DEFAULT — the overwhelming majority of wallets are
untiered and simply have no such account. Seeds bind it to
`creator_wallet`, so a caller cannot pass someone else's (cheaper) tier:
the PDA derivation would not match.

instructions.name: fund_escrow
docs: Fund the escrow with USDC

accounts.name: treasury_token_account
docs: Treasury token account — required only when the deal charges a fee.
Validated in the handler against deal.treasury + mint.

instructions.name: init_config
docs: Initialize the global platform config (fee + treasury + authority). Once.

instructions.name: migrate_config
docs: Grow the pre-tier Config PDA to the current layout (permissionless,
idempotent). MUST be run once after the tier upgrade before set_tiers,
set_user_tier, or a fee-bearing create_deal can load the config — the
old, shorter account otherwise fails to deserialize. Zero-fills the
appended bytes, which read back as "no tiers configured".

accounts.name: config
docs: deserialize, which is the whole reason we're here. Validated by hand:
PDA seeds, program ownership, and the Config discriminator.

instructions.name: migrate_deal
docs: Grow a pre-tier Deal account to the current layout (permissionless,
idempotent). Must be run on any deal created before the tier upgrade
before it can be funded, released, or refunded again — an old, shorter
account otherwise fails to deserialize. Zero-fills the new tail, which is
the correct legacy default (untiered, symmetric split).

accounts.name: payer
docs: Pays for the extra rent-exempt lamports the larger account needs.

accounts.name: deal
docs: too short to deserialize, which is the whole reason we're here. Validated
by hand: PDA seeds, program ownership, and the Deal discriminator.

instructions.name: refund
docs: Refund remaining funds to buyer (requires both signatures in ONE tx).
Superseded by `approve_refund` — kept for compatibility with any deal
mid-flight under the old flow.

instructions.name: release_milestone
docs: Release funds for a completed milestone

accounts.name: treasury_token_account
docs: Treasury token account — required only when the deal charges a fee.
Validated in the handler against deal.treasury + mint.

instructions.name: set_allowed_mints
docs: Replace the accepted-mint allowlist (authority only). Empty = any mint;
set [USDC,USDT,USDG] to restrict deal denomination (audit H-1).

instructions.name: set_authority
docs: Transfer the config authority to a new wallet (authority only)

instructions.name: set_fee
docs: Change the platform fee in basis points (authority only)

instructions.name: set_tiers
docs: Replace the pricing tier table (authority only). Repricing a tier is a
config change, never a redeploy; deals keep the rates they snapshotted.

instructions.name: set_treasury
docs: Change the treasury address (authority only)

instructions.name: set_user_tier
docs: Assign a wallet to a pricing tier (authority only). Creates or updates.

accounts.name: config
docs: Only the config authority may assign tiers — this is the pricing
control, so it must not be self-serve.

accounts.name: user_tier
docs: `init_if_needed` so one instruction both creates and updates an
assignment; re-running with a different tier_id is a promotion or
demotion rather than an error.

fields.name: version
docs: Layout version (audit #65 finding 5). First field, for the same reason
as Deal.version — dispatch on it before reading anything positional.

fields.name: authority
docs: The only wallet allowed to change fee settings.

fields.name: treasury
docs: Where platform fees are sent (owner of the treasury token account).
Pubkey::default() means "unset" → no fee is charged.

fields.name: fee_bps
docs: Default total fee in basis points (100 = 1%) for wallets with no tier.
Split half buyer / half seller, as it always has been.

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump seed

fields.name: tiers
docs: Pricing tiers, indexed by Tier.id. Empty = nobody is tiered and every
deal uses fee_bps. Sized generously up front (max 16): growing the cap
later would need another realloc.

fields.name: allowed_mints
docs: Mints a deal may be denominated in (audit H-1). Empty = accept ANY mint
(the pre-fix behavior, so an un-migrated Config keeps working) — set it
via `set_allowed_mints` to enforce USDC/USDT/USDG only. Appended AFTER
`tiers` to stay Borsh-positional: a zero-filled tail reads as an empty
vec, which migrate_config produces on an old account.

fields.name: _reserved
docs: Reserved padding (audit #65 finding 5). Future scalar config fields come
out of this block in place. (Vecs above already move the tail, so the
padding mainly guards fixed-size additions.)

fields.name: version
docs: Layout version (audit #65 finding 5). MUST be the first field so a reader
can dispatch on it before touching anything positional. Older on-chain
deals predate this field entirely — see the migration note at the bottom.

fields.name: deal_id
docs: Unique deal identifier

fields.name: buyer
docs: Buyer (funds the escrow)

fields.name: seller
docs: Seller (receives milestone payments)

fields.name: mint
docs: USDC mint address

fields.name: escrow_token_account
docs: Escrow token account (PDA-owned)

fields.name: total_amount
docs: Total deal amount in USDC (lamports)

fields.name: funded_amount
docs: Amount currently funded

fields.name: released_amount
docs: Amount already released

fields.name: status
docs: Deal status

fields.name: milestones
docs: Milestones (max 10)

fields.name: created_at
docs: Creation timestamp

fields.name: funded_at
docs: Timestamp when deal reached fully-funded status (0 = not yet funded)

fields.name: updated_at
docs: Last updated timestamp

fields.name: fee_bps
docs: Platform fee (bps) snapshotted from Config at creation. 0 = fee-free deal.
Frozen per-deal so later fee changes never affect in-flight deals.

fields.name: treasury
docs: Treasury snapshotted at creation (owner of the treasury token account the
buyer/seller fees are sent to). Pubkey::default() = no fee for this deal.

fields.name: buyer_fee_paid
docs: Whether the buyer's fee half has already been charged (once, at funding).

fields.name: buyer_refund_ok
docs: Mutual-refund approvals. Each party approves in their OWN transaction;
the refund executes once both are true. This replaces the old ceremony
where buyer and seller had to co-sign a single shared transaction, which
could not work in practice: a recent blockhash expires in ~90s and the
counterparty signs much later.

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump seed for PDA

fields.name: creator
docs: Who created the deal. Pubkey::default() = unknown → no tier applies. Not
inferable from `buyer`, which always signs create_deal.

fields.name: buyer_fee_bps
docs: Buyer's fee rate in bps of the buyer's side.

fields.name: seller_fee_bps
docs: Seller's fee rate in bps of the seller's side.

fields.name: asymmetric_fees
docs: Whether the two rates above are authoritative (vs the symmetric split).

fields.name: _reserved
docs: Reserved padding (audit #65 finding 5). New scalar fields are carved out
of THIS block in place, keeping every offset above it stable — so no
future addition can shift `bump` the way the history above did.

fields.name: description
docs: Milestone description

fields.name: amount
docs: Amount to release for this milestone

fields.name: status
docs: Status of this milestone

fields.name: confirmed_by
docs: Who confirmed completion (buyer confirms seller delivered)

fields.name: confirmed_at
docs: Confirmation timestamp

types.name: Tier
docs: Global platform config (PDA: seeds = ["config"]). Holds the changeable fee
rate, treasury, and the admin authority. A single instance for the program.
The fee is only ACTUALLY charged when fee_bps > 0 AND treasury is set — so
the program can be deployed and run fee-free until the treasury exists.
One pricing tier. The two rates are INDEPENDENT — a tier is any
(creator, counterparty) pair — so a tier can make the creator free while the
counterparty still pays their normal share, or shift the whole fee onto one
side. Pricing policy lives in data, not code: repricing is a `set_tiers`
call, never a redeploy.

fields.name: id
docs: Stable identifier referenced by UserTier.tier_id (0 = SSS, 1 = SS, …).

fields.name: creator_fee_bps
docs: Fee charged to the party who CREATED the deal, in bps of their side.

fields.name: counterparty_fee_bps
docs: Fee charged to the counterparty, in bps of their side.

types.name: UserTier
docs: Per-wallet tier assignment (PDA: seeds = ["tier", wallet]).
ABSENCE IS THE DEFAULT: a wallet with no UserTier account is untiered and
pays the standard fee. That costs nothing for the overwhelming majority of
users who aren't VIPs — only whitelisted wallets get an account. Revoking a
tier closes the account and returns the rent.

fields.name: wallet
docs: The wallet this assignment belongs to (also the PDA seed).

fields.name: tier_id
docs: Which Config.tiers entry applies to deals this wallet CREATES.

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump seed
